benchmark_explanation: This instance uses 4.7.2 B60-prefix nested scaling: B300 is a prefix of one deterministic B1440 common-pool append stream, not a freshly regenerated B300 instance.
The first 60 recourse blocks are byte-identical to the B60-good seed4 instance, and the first-stage capacity domain is frozen at U=(15,15) before applying the tail-continuous adapter.
This isolates scaling in the decomposable recourse side while preserving the B60 first-stage geometry, tail_start, and z-domain after tail-cont lifting.
The tail-continuous variant keeps the original integer capacity lattice as the main structure but adds a very small continuous flexibility interval at the highest capacity level.
Because u_i appears in Bz through zcap_i=y_i+u_i, a fixed-z enumerator cannot fully remove the global z coupling when a tail mode is active.
generator_notes: 4.7.2 NestedB60 enabled: B300 is the first 300 blocks of the deterministic B1440 common-pool append stream built from the B60-good seed4 prefix.
Append strategy used = common_pool; this reuses profile-preserving perturbed-copy expansion but removes target-dependent append streams, so B90/B120/B150/B180 are truly nested.
Frozen first-stage domain verified before tail-cont: U=(15,15); only the number of recourse blocks changes.

dcap_like_sun prefix expansion is enabled: first 60 x-blocks are the exact original generated B60 seed4 instance; blocks 61-300 are deterministic profile-preserving perturbed copies of those base blocks.
This is an instance-layer scaling option only. It does not modify P1/P2, the inner oracle, the Pessoa outer state machine, rho policy, LB/UB certificate, or final stopping logic.
The expansion isolates the effect of increasing decomposable x-block count while keeping z dimension, tier capacities/costs, budget, base task sizes/values, and the original hard B60 prefix fixed.
Perturbation jitter for appended blocks is 0.0300; setting --dcap_expand_jitter 0 creates exact repeated copies.

Expansion RNG seed used for appended blocks is 5711692; for B60/B120 this remains the original default stream; seed1 B80 keeps its previous tuned stream, and seed1 B100 is retuned to extend that same B80-good appended-block stream.
dcap_like_sun is a transparent, documented DCAP-like Sun benchmark family rather than a claim of exact SIPLIB/DCAP generator replication.

Its semantics follow the public DCAP skeleton: first-stage binary tier activations buy coarse resource-period capacity, while each local x-block solves a recourse assignment of realized task demand to purchased capacity under scenario-specific processing requirements.

Its structure follows Sun: z is a mild central coordination layer with resource-family × coarse-period × tier binaries, x = (x^1, ..., x^P) consists of many local recourse blocks, and all x-blocks decompose naturally once z is fixed.

The benchmark construction is reproducible from instance_seed and the explicitly recorded candidate seed; it never changes P1/P2/Gurobi algorithm logic. The active dcap_gurobi_profile is 'seed159_sunint'; the seed159 profiles target a Gurobi-facing sweet spot with material but not maximal disagreement.
Candidate override enabled: family seed=4, candidate index label=13, candidate seed=1346405564; exactly this B60 candidate is rebuilt.
The realized mild-z design uses 2 first-stage binaries (1 periods × 2 resource families × 1 tiers) and 60 local x-blocks.

The profile mix intentionally keeps a balanced-block majority while retaining early-focus, late-focus, and a small split-focus minority, so the family preserves competing pulls on z without forcing maximal local disagreement everywhere.

The realized z choice mode is 'integer_capacity' and the block weight mode is 'unit'. In EF-hard mode this is intentionally used to keep the z-pattern count small while making the x-side extensive form large.
The legacy CSV field n_scenarios is kept for backward compatibility; in dcap_like_sun it should be interpreted as the number of x-blocks / scenarios in the Sun-style block-angular family.
A-only PC1ProjectedMild family: it starts from the already-tested 5% Base60 mild heterogeneity and preserves that family mean and total Frobenius perturbation energy exactly.

The only geometric change is that all centered technology variation is projected onto the leading empirical PC1 direction; no focus labels, special blocks, P1/P2 outcomes, or reward changes enter the construction.

Nested descendants use only multiplicative scalar jitter on the source PC1 score and keep the original reward-jitter RNG stream; entrywise A jitter is disabled so rank-one technology geometry survives scaling.
4.7 tail-continuous DCAP adapter enabled: original z dimension 2 is replaced by y/b/u dimension 6; zcap=y+u enters Bz and the first-stage cost.
Tail domain per coordinate is {0,...,U_i-1} union [U_i,U_i+Delta] with Delta=0.1; tail starts are (15.0, 15.0).
RNC tail-u distance scale is 0.001; use smaller Delta or scale if B40 P1-only shows t=3/t=5 slowdown.

family_payload.dcap_pc1_projected_mild_definition: Rc=R0+0.05*(Rbar_raw-R0); centered raw C=U Sigma V^T; beta=0.05*||C||_F/sigma1; R_i=Rc+beta*(sigma1*u_i1)*v1. This exactly matches the old 5% mild family mean and total centered Frobenius energy, while centered technology deviation rank is at most one.
family_payload.dcap_pc1_projected_mild_inheritance_rule: nested child uses s_child=s_source*(1+xi), with xi taken from one entry of the legacy requirement-jitter RNG packet in [-jitter,jitter]; all packet draws are consumed to preserve the original reward-jitter stream; no entrywise A jitter
family_payload.dcap_pc1_projected_mild_expansion_note: Children inherit the exact source PC1 score. The original requirement-jitter RNG packet is consumed to preserve the reward-jitter stream, but no entrywise A jitter is applied.
family_payload.dcap_nested_b60_note: 4.7.2 nested B60 scaling: target instance is the first B blocks of one deterministic B60-to-pool common pool; the B60 first-stage domain is frozen before the tail-cont adapter. Base60 uses the mean/energy-matched PC1 projection of the old 5% mild technology; descendants use only 3%-level latent scalar score jitter and no entrywise A jitter.
family_payload.dcap_tail_note: 4.7 tail-continuous capacity domain: each original integer capacity coordinate is modeled as y_i,b_i,u_i with zcap_i=y_i+u_i and domain {0,...,U_i-1} U [U_i,U_i+Delta].
